conventions.convention: The twisting frames satisfy e_j^(k) = (Z_j/Z_i)^k e_i^(k). Section coefficients consequently transform by the inverse factor. O(0) is the trivial line bundle and its section sheaf is the structure sheaf.
Full AC is assumed. Analytic sheaf cohomology means right-derived global sections. The dimension range is 0 ≤ r ≤ 3, with P^0 a point; negative-twist conclusions require 1 ≤ r ≤ 3.

Čech indices increase in the order 0 < … < r, and the differential deletes the νth vertex with sign (-1)^ν. The mode homotopy inserts the least vertex outside the negative exponent set, with its ordered insertion sign.

Laurent modes have integer homogeneous exponents summing to k; a mode is allowed on U_I exactly when its negative exponent set is contained in I. Normal convergence means absolute and uniform convergence on every compact product subset.

Bundle-valued Dolbeault forms are smooth (0,q)-forms with the operator defined coefficientwise in holomorphic frames. Terms above the complex dimension are zero, and the degree-zero quotient has zero denominator. The comparison is analytic sheaf cohomology versus smooth Dolbeault cohomology, not algebraic-to-analytic GAGA.

load_bearing.statement: Under full AC, the standard projective intersections admit unique normally convergent homogeneous mixed Laurent–Taylor expansions. Restrictions preserve modes, and every nonempty proper negative exponent set has the stated convergent insertion contraction. The intersections are acyclic for O(k), k ∈ {0,-1,-r-1}. Consequently H^0(P^r,O)=C and H^q(P^r,O)=0 for q>0 when 0≤r≤3; H^0(P^r,O(-1))=0 and H^r(P^r,O(-r-1))≅C when 1≤r≤3.

Assume full AC. For r∈{0,1,2,3} and every finite-rank holomorphic vector bundle E on X=P^r(C), the canonical comparison induced by the smooth Dolbeault resolution is an isomorphism H^q(X,O(E))≅H^q_dbar(X,E) for every q≥0. For the trivial line bundle, H^0(P^r,O)=C and H^q(P^r,O)=0 for q>0.

For r≥1 and k∈Z, O_P^r(k) is obtained by gluing U_i×C with local frames satisfying e_j^(k)=(Z_j/Z_i)^k e_i^(k) on U_i∩U_j. Its section sheaf assigns holomorphic sections to each open set, and O_P^r:=O_P^r(0) is the structure sheaf.

seams_checked.note: The projective GAGA theorem's A5 uses precisely the scalar structure-sheaf values in dimensions 0–3. Its proof retains full AC and derives further twisting-sheaf conclusions separately; it does not assume them from this supplier.

The finite-but-nonzero example uses the twisting definition with e_1=z^(-2)e_0. Its two-chart coboundary and surviving z^(-1) coefficient agree with that convention; its cohomology computation is supplied separately.

The fibre lemma uses the Laurent supplier at r=1 for O(-1) and O(-2), and the analytic comparison converts those sheaf groups to smooth Dolbeault groups. The injective-edge lemma and vanishing theorem use the finite-rank holomorphic-bundle comparison on P^3 under full AC, without claiming algebraic GAGA.

The hyperplane sequences preserve the twisting-frame convention. The analytic-twist lemma derives negative-twist vanishings from the scalar values in dimensions 0–3 and exact sequences. Internal positivity uses H^0(P^1,O)=C to identify sections of a trivial finite-rank bundle with constant vectors. The normal-form theorem retains full AC and the same scalar interface.
